<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22Re%5C%3A+%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Re%5C%3A+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+WebTransport+receive+stream%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">Re: [blink-dev] Re: Intent to Ship: WebTransport receive stream</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Mike+Taylor%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Mike Taylor</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261028" rel="nofollow">Wed, 28 Oct 2026 19:46:04 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM3
On 10/28/26 5:20 a.m., Chris Harrelson wrote: </pre><blockquote style="border-left: #5555EE solid 0.2em; margin: 0em; padding-left: 0.85em"><pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM2</pre><pre></pre><tt>On Tue, Oct 27, 2026 at 7:03 PM Alex Russell </tt><tt><<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="92e1fefbf5fae6feebbcbcbcd2f1fae0fdfffbe7ffbcfde0f5">[email protected]</a>> wrote: </tt><pre style="margin: 0em;">
LGTM1; love to see these practical additions!
On Wednesday, October 21, 2026 at 6:31:37 PM UTC-7 Chromestatus wrote:
*Contact emails* <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="245246565d4c4d0a0a0a64494d47564b574b42500a474b49">[email protected]</a>
*Explainer* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/372">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/issues/372</a> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/395">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/395</a>
*Specification* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#webtransportreceivestream">https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#webtransportreceivestream</a>
*Summary* Adds the standardized WebTransportReceiveStream interface, a ReadableStream subclass used for incoming unidirectional streams and the readable side of bidirectional streams. Its getStats() method returns per-stream byte counters: bytesReceived reports bytes received from the network, while bytesRead reports bytes delivered to the application.
*Blink component* Blink>Network>WebTransport
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22">https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22</a>>
*Web Feature ID* webtransport <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport">https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport</a>>
*Motivation* Incoming WebTransport streams have historically been exposed as generic ReadableStream objects in Chromium. The WebTransport specification defines a dedicated WebTransportReceiveStream subclass with stream-specific statistics. Applications that receive large or latency-sensitive streams need to distinguish bytes received by the browser from bytes actually consumed by JavaScript. This helps diagnose application backpressure, buffering, and slow-consumer behavior. Exposing the standardized subclass also aligns the runtime type of incoming streams with the WebTransport specification and other browser engines.
*Initial public proposal* /No information provided/
*TAG review* /No information provided/
*TAG review status* Not applicable
*Goals for experimentation* None
*Risks*
*Interoperability and Compatibility* Enabling this feature changes incoming unidirectional streams and the readable side of bidirectional streams from plain ReadableStream objects to WebTransportReceiveStream objects. Reading remains compatible, and the objects remain instanceof ReadableStream, but applications that compare the exact constructor or prototype may observe a change. Firefox and Safari already expose WebTransportReceiveStream, so this aligns Chrome’s stream type with those browsers.
/Gecko/: Under consideration (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/webidl/WebTransportSendReceiveStream.webidl">https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/webidl/WebTransportSendReceiveStream.webidl</a>) Partial implementation. Firefox ships WebTransportReceiveStream and exposes getStats(), but getStats() currently rejects with NotSupportedError, so receive stream statistics are not implemented. Implementation
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/webtransport/api/WebTransportReceiveStream.cpp">https://searchfox.org/mozilla-central/source/dom/webtransport/api/WebTransportReceiveStream.cpp</a>
/WebKit/: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://commits.webkit.org/300850@main">https://commits.webkit.org/300850@main</a>) WebKit-7624.1.16 implements WebTransportReceiveStream and pipes real receive-stream statistics through WebCore and the network process. WebTransport shipped in Safari 26.4. Implementation -
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/WebKit-7624.1.16/Source/WebCore/Modules/webtransport/WebTransportReceiveStream.cpp#L54-L65">https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/WebKit-7624.1.16/Source/WebCore/Modules/webtransport/WebTransportReceiveStream.cpp#L54-L65</a>
/Web developers/: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a>) The Interop 2026 WebTransport proposal received 28 positive reactions. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
/Other signals/:
*Ergonomics* getStats() asynchronously returns a snapshot with bytesReceived and bytesRead. bytesRead is expected to be less than or equal to bytesReceived. Chromium preserves final counters when streams finish, are reset or cancelled, or when the Mojo connection disconnects. The interface is not constructible directly; applications obtain it from incomingUnidirectionalStreams or from the readable side of a bidirectional stream. Chromium's IDL currently types WebTransportBidirectionalStream.readable as ReadableStream because Blink cannot conditionally change an IDL attribute type behind a runtime flag, although the returned object is a WebTransportReceiveStream when the feature is enabled.
*Activation* Activation is automatic for sites using incoming WebTransport streams; no server change or opt-in is required. Existing code that treats these objects as ReadableStream continues to work because WebTransportReceiveStream is a subclass. The runtime type and prototype are observably different, so code that relies on an exact ReadableStream constructor or prototype could behave differently. Feature detection using "getStats" in stream is recommended.
*Security* The API adds no network capability and exposes no peer address, credentials, or payload contents. It reports byte counters for a stream already available to the calling origin. These values reveal only the amount of data received by the browser and consumed by that application.
*WebView application risks*
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications?
Low. This is an additive API on existing WebTransport streams and does not change connection establishment or network behavior. WebView code that does not inspect the stream's exact runtime type is unaffected.
*Debuggability* Developers can inspect incoming streams and call getStats() from the DevTools Console. The returned bytesReceived and bytesRead values help distinguish network delivery from application consumption. DevTools does not currently provide a dedicated per-WebTransport-stream statistics UI.
*Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)?* Yes
*Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md">https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md</a>>?* Yes <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/receive-stream-stats.https.any.html">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/receive-stream-stats.https.any.html</a>
*Flag name on about://flags* enable-experimental-web-platform-features
*Finch feature name* WebTransportReceiveStream
*Rollout plan* Will ship enabled for all users
*Requires code in //chrome?* False
*Tracking bug* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/568317222">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/568317222</a>
*Availability expectation* The interface is defined in the W3C WebTransport specification. WebKit implements WebTransportReceiveStream and real receive-stream statistics. Firefox exposes WebTransportReceiveStream, but its getStats() implementation currently rejects with NotSupportedError. Implementations are expected to converge through the Interop 2026 WebTransport focus area.
*Adoption expectation* Expected to be adopted by WebTransport applications that monitor per stream throughput, buffering, or slow-consumer behavior. Code that only reads from incoming streams does not need to change.
*Adoption plan* Adoption is expected to occur organically through WebTransport documentation, examples, and client library support. Developers can progressively enhance existing code by feature-detecting getStats().
*Non-OSS dependencies*
Does the feature depend on any code or APIs outside the Chromium open source repository and its open-source dependencies to function?
No
*Estimated milestones* Shipping on desktop 158 DevTrial on desktop 155 Shipping on Android 158 DevTrial on Android 155 Shipping on WebView 158
*Anticipated spec changes*
Open questions about a feature may be a source of future web compat or interop issues. Please list open issues (e.g. links to known github issues in the project for the feature specification) whose resolution may introduce web compat/interop risk (e.g., changing to naming or structure of the API in a non-backward-compatible way).
None known for the WebTransportReceiveStream interface or the bytesReceived and bytesRead members.

<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22Re%5C%3A+%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Experiment%5C%3A+Private+Verification+Tokens%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">Re: [blink-dev] Intent to Experiment: Private Verification Tokens</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22%27Aykut+Bulut%27+via+blink%5C-dev%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">'Aykut Bulut' via blink-dev</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261030" rel="nofollow">Fri, 30 Oct 2026 16:36:39 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Hi all,
Thanks for your patience and feedback/questions. First, we wanted to update this group: based on a discussion with the Privacy team, we are considering further restricting this API to the user’s configured default search engine (DSE) for the duration of the OT. We are talking to (and looking for) partners on this, and are open to exploring alternative privacy mitigations. More on this in our response to question 4.2 in Daniel’s email.</pre><pre>
Response to questions from Daniel:
1. Yes, this is something we are very conscious of and want to prevent. PVT issuers will be required to register on GitHub (see process documentation <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/GoogleChrome/private-tokens/blob/main/PVT-Registration.md">https://github.com/GoogleChrome/private-tokens/blob/main/PVT-Registration.md</a>>) and declare their use-case, and we recommend that the API only be used for purposes of bot detection and ultimately reducing CAPTCHA-style friction. While this is not a technical guarantee, we think the public accountability will discourage abuse of the API.
We think understanding why sites are asking the user to log in will be part of the progress. Are they doing this because they would like to serve only logged in users or they can not distinguish anonymous users from a scraper bot? The question is whether they would be more willing to allow access to anonymous browsing if they can trust the traffic more.
2. Tokens can only carry 1 bit of information, are unlinkable to the issuance context, and are generally designed to prevent re-identification of individual users. Additional information about our privacy mitigations is documented here <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/private-verification-tokens#privacy-considerations">https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/private-verification-tokens#privacy-considerations</a>> .
3. Current implementation can be used by other Chromium based browsers.
4.1 How do we know the user wants to make that sacrifice?
In the context of previous work to build private anti-abuse technologies, we had conducted some user research to understand user sentiment on the privacy vs. anti-abuse trade-offs. A key finding from that study was that “Users acknowledge the trade-off between privacy and anti-abuse mechanisms, and are more willing to accept the trade-off in high-security contexts and when they trust the organization”. While it is difficult to determine the security-relevance of the website, we think that the browser could use heuristics to determine trust in the organization. For example, we believe that users likely have higher trust in their DSE, and that it could serve as a reasonable heuristic for the OT. Additionally, the frequency of interaction with the DSE increases the need to lower friction.
4.2 Should it be an opt-in feature?
We agree with the concerns raised by the privacy reviewer and folks in this thread. Based on discussion with the privacy reviewer - for the duration of the OT, we are considering limiting the API to the user’s configured DSE. We think this is a worthy compromise to enable OT.
Based on whether the OT validates the usefulness of the API and interest from partners, we intend to explore additional privacy mitigations such as an explicit opt-in through a new capability-element (similar to <a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/feature/5153829504024576">https://chromestatus.com/feature/5153829504024576</a>) per origin.
We think convincing partners to include such an element to their captcha page will be easier if we can show some value that what we propose works through OT.
5. Could you clarify which efforts you are referring to? Is this about the MoLE work <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/Moderation-of-unLinkable-Endorsements/internet-drafts">https://github.com/Moderation-of-unLinkable-Endorsements/internet-drafts</a>> that recently kicked off in the IETF?
6. Please see our response to 4.2 above.
Response to Derrick,
> "unavoidably transfer knowledge that the user is a prior visitor to the site. The user's identity may be successfully masked, but the existence of a relationship to the first party is not."
We created issue #12 <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/private-verification-tokens/issues/12">https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/private-verification-tokens/issues/12</a>> to update the privacy section.
> I suggest that treating PVTs as a site level permission would be appropriate. Even if browser implementations decide that this should be default-allow, a site-level permission provides some site-level control in the event of low trust or a specific need. When I compare to other available site permissions, this seems like it would fit in well.
Thank you. We are tracking this in issue #13 <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/private-verification-tokens/issues/13">https://github.com/explainers-by-googlers/private-verification-tokens/issues/13</a>> .
Aykut & Kaustubha

entry.summary: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransportError API alignment and serialization
entry.content:
<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+WebTransportError+API+alignment+and+serialization%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransportError API alignment and serialization</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Chromestatus%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Chromestatus</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261103" rel="nofollow">Tue, 03 Nov 2026 14:21:14 -0800</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Contact emails <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="49242627202a6767670924202a3b263a262f3d672a2624">[email protected]</a> </pre><pre>
Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md</a>
Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#web-transport-error-interface">https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#web-transport-error-interface</a>
Design docs
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebTransportError">https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebTransportError</a> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/webtransport">https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/webtransport</a>
Summary Updates Chromium WebTransportError to match the current WebTransport specification. Adds the standard (message, options) constructor while preserving the shipped dictionary constructor for compatibility; carries the full unsigned-long stream error code end to end; and makes WebTransportError structured-clonable while preserving its message, source, and nullable error code. Serialization is enabled by default behind a writer-side runtime kill switch, while decoding remains permanently enabled for persisted values.
Blink component Blink>Network>WebTransport
Web Feature ID webtransport
Motivation Chromium's shipped WebTransportError implementation predates the current WebTransport specification. It accepts a legacy dictionary-only constructor, narrows outgoing application stream error codes to 8 bits despite the API exposing an unsigned long, and does not support the structured serialization required by the specification. The change aligns Chromium with the standardized API and improves WebTransport interoperability. The legacy constructor remains available so existing Chromium applications continue to work.
Initial public proposal No information provided
TAG review <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/669">https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/669</a>
TAG review status Not applicable
Goals for experimentation None
Risks
Interoperability and Compatibility Interoperability risk Low. The constructor, WebTransportErrorOptions dictionary, unsigned-long streamErrorCode, source attribute, and serialization behavior are defined in the W3C WebTransport specification and covered by Web Platform Tests. Mozilla implemented the same constructor and full-width stream error-code behavior and contributed the relevant WPT coverage: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63842">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63842</a> Compatibility risk Low. Chromium's shipped dictionary constructor is retained as a compatibility overload, including its existing octet clamping and handling of trailing arguments. Existing calls therefore continue to work. The intentional behavior changes are that application stream error codes above 255 are no longer truncated, and structured-cloning a WebTransportError now succeeds instead of throwing DataCloneError. Code that deliberately depended on either non-standard behavior could observe a difference.
Gecko: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2009530">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2009530</a>)
WebKit: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=305224">https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=305224</a>)
Web developers: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a>) The Interop 2026 WebTransport proposal received 28 👍 reactions. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
Other signals:
Ergonomics Low. The standard constructor follows familiar Error and DOMException patterns: new WebTransportError("message", { source: "stream", streamErrorCode: 70000 }); Existing Chromium dictionary-style construction remains supported. Structured cloning preserves the WebTransportError subtype and its WebTransport-specific properties instead of reducing it to a generic exception or rejecting it.
Activation Low. The standard constructor and full-width stream error-code support correct existing non-conforming behavior while preserving Chromium's legacy constructor. Structured serialization is newly observable behavior. It is controlled by the WebTransportErrorSerialization runtime feature, which is enabled by default but retained as a writer-side kill switch. The deserializer is intentionally always enabled so WebTransportError values already stored in IndexedDB or other structured-clone storage remain readable if writing is disabled. The implementation is covered by focused Blink and Network Service tests and the Mozilla Web Platform Tests.
Security Low. The change does not grant additional network access, expose new server or user information, or weaken WebTransport's secure-context requirement. Structured cloning copies only the WebTransportError subtype, DOMString message, source enum, and nullable unsigned 32-bit stream error code. The versioned decoder validates the format version, enum discriminants, presence flags, string code units, and payload completeness before constructing an object.
WebView application risks
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? Low risk. This aligns the existing WebTransportError API with the current specification. Existing error values from 0–255 retain identical behavior, the legacy constructor remains supported, and ordinary creation, throwing, and catching are unchanged. Structured cloning changes from throwing DataCloneError to succeeding. Serialization writes are protected by a kill switch, while the reader remains enabled for compatibility with previously persisted data.
Debuggability No feature-specific DevTools support is required. Developers can inspect WebTransportError.name, message, source, and streamErrorCode in the DevTools Console. Existing WebTransport diagnostics, NetLog, Network Service logging, and QUIC logging remain available for tracing the underlying stream error.
Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)? Yes
Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests? Yes <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a>
DevTrial instructions <a rel="nofollow" href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebTransportError#examples">https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebTransportError#examples</a>
Flag name on about://flags enable-experimental-web-platform-features
Finch feature name WebTransportErrorSerialization
Non-finch justification Ships enabled to 100%. The runtime feature is retained as a serialization kill switch, not for a gradual Finch experiment.
Rollout plan Will ship enabled for all users
Requires code in //chrome? False
Tracking bug <a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/577073049">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/577073049</a>
Measurement A Blink UseCounter will measure use of Chromium's legacy dictionary WebTransportError constructor so that its compatibility impact can be evaluated before any future deprecation. The standardized constructor, uint32 stream error-code propagation, and serialization behavior are validated through WPT and Chromium integration tests. No dedicated UMA metric is planned for serialization because it is a deterministic structured-clone capability and does not change network policy or resource allocation.
Availability expectation Firefox has implemented the aligned WebTransportError API, including structured serialization. WebKit supports WebTransport and has landed the updated constructor and stream error-code behavior, although WebTransportError-specific structured serialization has not yet been confirmed. Remaining interoperability is being tracked through Interop 2026.
Adoption expectation Existing WebTransport applications benefit automatically from the corrected constructor and full-width stream error codes. Applications using workers, postMessage(), structuredClone(), or persistent structured-clone storage can propagate WebTransportError values without custom conversion. No migration is required for existing users
Adoption plan Ship the standards-aligned behavior by default, maintain Web Platform Test coverage, and track cross-browser implementation through the Interop 2026 WebTransport effort. This is primarily a compatibility and interoperability correction, so no separate developer migration campaign is necessary.
Estimated milestones
Shipping on desktop 159
DevTrial on desktop 159
Shipping on Android 159
DevTrial on Android 159
Shipping on WebView 159
Anticipated spec changes
Open questions about a feature may be a source of future web compat or interop issues. Please list open issues (eg links to known github issues in the project for the feature specification) whose resolution may introduce web compat/interop risk (eg, changing to naming or structure of the API in a non-backward-compatible way). None anticipated. This implements the current WebTransport specification rather than introducing a new API design. No known open specification issues are expected to require incompatible changes to this API.

Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/tc39/proposal-regexp-buffer-boundaries">https://github.com/tc39/proposal-regexp-buffer-boundaries</a>

The standard SCTP connection establishment requires a handshake that introduces latency. A new Internet draft specifies a method to accelerate the datachannel establishment by embedding the SCTP initialization parameters within the Session Description Protocol (SDP) offer/answer exchange. This reduces the time required to open a data channel by up to two network round-trip times.

*Summary* Updates navigator.mediaSession.setMicrophoneActive() and navigator.mediaSession.setCameraActive() to return a Promise<undefined> instead of undefined, matching the W3C Media Session specification. In a fully active document, the returned promise resolves with undefined; if the associated document is not fully active, it returns a promise rejected with an InvalidStateError DOMException.
*Blink component* Blink>Media>Session
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3EMedia%3ESession%22">https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3EMedia%3ESession%22</a>>

*Motivation* When MediaSession.setMicrophoneActive() and MediaSession.setCameraActive() were originally specified and shipped in Chrome 93, their WebIDL return type was void (undefined). The W3C Media Session specification was subsequently updated (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/mediasession/pull/312">https://github.com/w3c/mediasession/pull/312</a>) so that both methods return Promise<undefined> to support user agents that apply a capture pause policy or prompt the user asynchronously. Updating Chromium's implementation to return Promise<undefined> aligns Chrome with the W3C Media Session specification and fixes 4 failing subtests in WPT's mediasession/idlharness.window.html.
*Initial public proposal* /No information provided/
*TAG review* N/A — This is a minor spec-compliance update to the return type (undefined -> Promise<undefined>) of two already-shipped MediaSession methods, already specified in the W3C Media Session Working Draft (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/mediasession/pull/312">https://github.com/w3c/mediasession/pull/312</a>) and shipped in Safari.
*TAG review status* Not applicable
*Goals for experimentation* None
*Risks*
*Interoperability and Compatibility* Compatibility risk is very low. Existing callers that ignore the return value of setMicrophoneActive() and setCameraActive() are unaffected because the returned promise always resolves with undefined in an active document (so fire-and-forget callers will not encounter unhandled promise rejections). The promise only rejects with InvalidStateError when called on a MediaSession whose associated Document is no longer fully active (such as a detached iframe), or with TypeError when called with too few arguments or an invalid receiver per WebIDL rules for promise-returning operations. Interoperability is improved, as Safari already ships Promise<undefined> for both methods and Firefox is implementing the same WebIDL signature.
/Gecko/: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/504">https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/504</a>)
/WebKit/: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=277421">https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=277421</a>) Shipped in Safari 18.4

Adds the standard (message, options) constructor while preserving the shipped dictionary constructor for compatibility; carries the full unsigned-long stream error code end to end; and makes WebTransportError structured-clonable while preserving its message, source, and nullable error code. Serialization is enabled by default behind a writer-side runtime kill switch, while decoding remains permanently enabled for persisted values.
*Blink component* Blink>Network>WebTransport
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22">https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22</a>>
*Web Feature ID* webtransport <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport">https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport</a>>
*Motivation* Chromium's shipped WebTransportError implementation predates the current WebTransport specification. It accepts a legacy dictionary-only constructor, narrows outgoing application stream error codes to 8 bits despite the API exposing an unsigned long, and does not support the structured serialization required by the specification. The change aligns Chromium with the standardized API and improves WebTransport interoperability. The legacy constructor remains available so existing Chromium applications continue to work.
*Initial public proposal* /No information provided/
*TAG review* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/669">https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/669</a>
*TAG review status* Not applicable
*Goals for experimentation* None
*Risks*
*Interoperability and Compatibility* Interoperability risk Low. The constructor, WebTransportErrorOptions dictionary, unsigned-long streamErrorCode, source attribute, and serialization behavior are defined in the W3C WebTransport specification and covered by Web Platform Tests. Mozilla implemented the same constructor and full-width stream error-code behavior and contributed the relevant WPT coverage: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63842">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63842</a> Compatibility risk Low. Chromium's shipped dictionary constructor is retained as a compatibility overload, including its existing octet clamping and handling of trailing arguments. Existing calls therefore continue to work. The intentional behavior changes are that application stream error codes above 255 are no longer truncated, and structured-cloning a WebTransportError now succeeds instead of throwing DataCloneError. Code that deliberately depended on either non-standard behavior could observe a difference.
/Gecko/: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2009530">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2009530</a>)
/WebKit/: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=305224">https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=305224</a>)
/Web developers/: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a>) The Interop 2026 WebTransport proposal received 28 👍 reactions. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
/Other signals/:
*Ergonomics* Low. The standard constructor follows familiar Error and DOMException patterns: new WebTransportError("message", { source: "stream", streamErrorCode: 70000 }); Existing Chromium dictionary-style construction remains supported. Structured cloning preserves the WebTransportError subtype and its WebTransport-specific properties instead of reducing it to a generic exception or rejecting it.
*Activation* Low. The standard constructor and full-width stream error-code support correct existing non-conforming behavior while preserving Chromium's legacy constructor. Structured serialization is newly observable behavior. It is controlled by the WebTransportErrorSerialization runtime feature, which is enabled by default but retained as a writer-side kill switch. The deserializer is intentionally always enabled so WebTransportError values already stored in IndexedDB or other structured-clone storage remain readable if writing is disabled. The implementation is covered by focused Blink and Network Service tests and the Mozilla Web Platform Tests.
*Security* Low. The change does not grant additional network access, expose new server or user information, or weaken WebTransport's secure-context requirement. Structured cloning copies only the WebTransportError subtype, DOMString message, source enum, and nullable unsigned 32-bit stream error code. The versioned decoder validates the format version, enum discriminants, presence flags, string code units, and payload completeness before constructing an object.
*WebView application risks*
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications?
Low risk. This aligns the existing WebTransportError API with the current specification. Existing error values from 0–255 retain identical behavior, the legacy constructor remains supported, and ordinary creation, throwing, and catching are unchanged. Structured cloning changes from throwing DataCloneError to succeeding. Serialization writes are protected by a kill switch, while the reader remains enabled for compatibility with previously persisted data.
*Debuggability* No feature-specific DevTools support is required. Developers can inspect WebTransportError.name, message, source, and streamErrorCode in the DevTools Console. Existing WebTransport diagnostics, NetLog, Network Service logging, and QUIC logging remain available for tracing the underlying stream error.
*Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)?* Yes
*Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md">https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md</a>>?* Yes
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a>>
*DevTrial instructions* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebTransportError#examples">https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebTransportError#examples</a>
*Flag name on about://flags* enable-experimental-web-platform-features
*Finch feature name* WebTransportErrorSerialization
*Non-finch justification* Ships enabled to 100%. The runtime feature is retained as a serialization kill switch, not for a gradual Finch experiment.
*Rollout plan* Will ship enabled for all users
*Requires code in //chrome?* False
*Tracking bug* <a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/577073049">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/577073049</a>
*Measurement* A Blink UseCounter will measure use of Chromium's legacy dictionary WebTransportError constructor so that its compatibility impact can be evaluated before any future deprecation. The standardized constructor, uint32 stream error-code propagation, and serialization behavior are validated through WPT and Chromium integration tests. No dedicated UMA metric is planned for serialization because it is a deterministic structured-clone capability and does not change network policy or resource allocation.
*Availability expectation* Firefox has implemented the aligned WebTransportError API, including structured serialization. WebKit supports WebTransport and has landed the updated constructor and stream error-code behavior, although WebTransportError-specific structured serialization has not yet been confirmed. Remaining interoperability is being tracked through Interop 2026.
*Adoption expectation* Existing WebTransport applications benefit automatically from the corrected constructor and full-width stream error codes. Applications using workers, postMessage(), structuredClone(), or persistent structured-clone storage can propagate WebTransportError values without custom conversion. No migration is required for existing users
*Adoption plan* Ship the standards-aligned behavior by default, maintain Web Platform Test coverage, and track cross-browser implementation through the Interop 2026 WebTransport effort. This is primarily a compatibility and interoperability correction, so no separate developer migration campaign is necessary.
*Estimated milestones* Shipping on desktop 159 DevTrial on desktop 159 Shipping on Android 159 DevTrial on Android 159 Shipping on WebView 159
*Anticipated spec changes*
Open questions about a feature may be a source of future web compat or interop issues. Please list open issues (e.g. links to known github issues in the project for the feature specification) whose resolution may introduce web compat/interop risk (e.g., changing to naming or structure of the API in a non-backward-compatible way).
None anticipated. This implements the current WebTransport specification rather than introducing a new API design. No known open specification issues are expected to require incompatible changes to this API.

From: <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="17757b7e797c3a73726157747f65787a7e627a39786570">[email protected]</a> <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="5436383d3a3f7930312214373c263b393d21397a3b2633">[email protected]</a>> On Behalf Of Chromestatus Sent: Thursday, November 5, 2026 9:37 AM To: <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="c5a7a9acabaee8a1a0b385a6adb7aaa8acb0a8ebaab7a2">[email protected]</a> Cc: Daniel Clark <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="97f3f6f9b9b9b9d7fafef4e5f8e4f8f1e3b9f4f8fa">[email protected]</a>>; <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="ff8d96d1d1d1bf98909098939ad19c9092">[email protected]</a>; <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="d5a6b9bcb2bda1b9acfbfbfb95b6bda7bab8bca0b8fbbaa7b2">[email protected]</a>; Viktoriya Bryhider <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="4a3c28383322236464640a272329382539252c3e64292527">[email protected]</a>> Subject: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport connection statistics</pre><pre>
Contact emails <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="433521313a2b2a6d6d6d032e2a20312c302c25376d202c2e">[email protected]</a><<a rel="nofollow" href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#1b6d79696273723535355b767278697468747d6f35787476">mailto:<span class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="ef998d9d968786c1c1c1af82868c9d809c80899bc18c8082">[email protected]</span></a>> Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#stats">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#stats</a> Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#dictdef-webtransportconnectionstats">https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#dictdef-webtransportconnectionstats</a> Design docs
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebTransport/getStats">https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/WebTransport/getStats</a> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#web-transport-connection-stats">https://w3c.github.io/webtransport/#web-transport-connection-stats</a> Summary WebTransport.getStats() provides asynchronous statistics for an existing connection: round-trip time measurements when available, an estimated sending rate when available, and counts of expired, lost, and dropped datagrams. Statistics remain accessible after the connection closes. Chromium does not currently expose connection byte or packet totals. Blink component Blink>Network>WebTransport<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22">https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22</a>> Web Feature ID webtransport<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport">https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport</a>> Motivation WebTransport applications need to distinguish connection latency, congestion, and datagram loss or expiration from application-side delays. A single asynchronous call exposes a snapshot of the existing connection's health to help developers adapt sending behavior and troubleshoot problems. It does not create a connection or change how application data is transmitted. Initial public proposal No information provided TAG review <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/1212#issuecomment-5071009850">https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/1212#issuecomment-5071009850</a> TAG review status Issues addressed Goals for experimentation None Risks
Interoperability and Compatibility This is an additive method on an existing WebTransport object: existing code is unaffected if it does not use the new method. Developers must check for method support and handle a rejection or missing dictionary members when working across browsers. Firefox and Safari expose getStats(), but implementation maturity and returned fields vary between all browsers. The WebTransport specification currently defines connection byte/packet counters (bytesSent, bytesSentOverhead, bytesAcknowledged, packetsSent, bytesLost, packetsLost, bytesReceived, packetsReceived) and atSendCapacity; Chromium does not expose these members. Applications should check for optional members rather than assume that every browser returns the same subset.
Gecko: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/158#apis">https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/158#apis</a>) WebTransport.getStats() shipped in Firefox 158, released October 13, 2026.
WebKit: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/WebKit-7625.2.8/Source/WebKit/NetworkProcess/webtransport/cocoa/NetworkTransportSessionCocoa.mm#L410-L413">https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/WebKit-7625.2.8/Source/WebKit/NetworkProcess/webtransport/cocoa/NetworkTransportSessionCocoa.mm#L410-L413</a>) Safari 27.2 exposes WebTransport.getStats(), but its WebKit(7625.2.8) implementation returns default-initialized connection statistics. WebKit main has since added bytesSent and bytesReceived counters.
Web developers: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a>) The Interop 2026 WebTransport proposal received 28 positive reactions. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
Other signals: Ergonomics Values are asynchronous snapshots, not continuously updated measurements. RTT fields are in milliseconds; estimatedSendRate is in bits per second and can be null when no estimate is available. Activation There is no distinct activation risk identified for WebTransport.getStats(). Enabling it exposes an additive method; sites that do not call it keep their existing WebTransport behavior. Security The method returns aggregate connection information for a WebTransport object the caller already owns; it does not disclose payloads or peer credentials and does not add a new connection capability. RTT and estimated send rate can reveal characteristics of a user's network and help fingerprint or correlate activity. The WebTransport spec limits disclosure of connection and datagram counters on connections subject to pooling while permitting selected pooled-connection measurements such as RTT and estimated send rate. WebView application risks
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? Low. This is an additive API on existing WebTransport API and does not change connection establishment or network behavior.
Debuggability Applications can inspect getStats() results from script or the DevTools Console. No dedicated DevTools connection-statistics UI is required for the API to work. Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)? Yes Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md">https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md</a>>? Yes <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stats.https.any.html">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/stats.https.any.html</a> Flag name on about://flags enable-experimental-web-platform-features Finch feature name WebTransportStats Rollout plan Will ship enabled for all users Requires code in //chrome? False Tracking bug <a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/573538454">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/573538454</a> Availability expectation Firefox 158 and Safari 26.4 expose WebTransport.getStats(), although implementation maturity and available dictionary fields differ. Adoption expectation Adoption is expected primarily among WebTransport applications that monitor network performance or datagram delivery. Non-OSS dependencies
Does the feature depend on any code or APIs outside the Chromium open source repository and its open-source dependencies to function? No Estimated milestones Shipping on desktop 159 DevTrial on desktop 124 Shipping on Android 159 DevTrial on Android 124 Shipping on WebView 159
Anticipated spec changes

entry.title: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport reliability attributes
entry.summary: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport reliability attributes
entry.content:
<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+WebTransport+reliability+attributes%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] Intent to Ship: WebTransport reliability attributes</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Chromestatus%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Chromestatus</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261007" rel="nofollow">Wed, 07 Oct 2026 10:23:32 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Contact emails <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="0d7f642323234d6e657f626064786023627f6a">[email protected]</a> </pre><pre>
Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#transport-modes">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/blob/main/explainer.md#transport-modes</a>
Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#dom-webtransport-reliability">https://www.w3.org/TR/webtransport/#dom-webtransport-reliability</a>
Summary Adds the WebTransport.reliability instance attribute and static WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly attribute. These APIs indicate whether the user agent supports WebTransport over exclusively reliable connections and whether an established session supports unreliable transport such as datagrams. In Chromium, reliability initially returns "pending" and changes to "supports-unreliable" after an HTTP/3 WebTransport connection is established. Since Chromium does not currently support HTTP/2 fallback, WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly returns false; any successfully established session uses HTTP/3 and supports unreliable datagrams.
Blink component Blink>Network>WebTransport
Web Feature ID webtransport
Motivation WebTransport may operate over connections with different reliability capabilities. Applications such as games, interactive media, and real-time collaboration tools need to know whether unreliable datagrams are available before selecting their transport strategy. WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly reports whether the user agent supports WebTransport over exclusively reliable connections. The per-session reliability attribute is "pending" while connecting and becomes "reliable-only" or "supports-unreliable" once the transport is known. Chromium currently implements WebTransport over HTTP/3 with unreliable datagram support, so established sessions report "supports-unreliable" and supportsReliableOnly returns false.
Initial public proposal <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/385">https://github.com/w3c/webtransport/pull/385</a>
TAG review This is a small incremental implementation of attributes already defined in the existing W3C WebTransport specification. It does not introduce a new API design or Chromium-specific extension
TAG review status Not applicable
Goals for experimentation None
Risks
Interoperability and Compatibility Compatibility risk is low because both attributes are additive and do not change existing WebTransport behavior. Interoperability risk is low because the attributes and their "pending" , "reliable-only" , and "supports-unreliable" values are defined by the W3C WebTransport specification. Equivalent APIs are implemented or partially implemented in WebKit and Firefox, and WebTransport is an Interop 2026 focus area.
Gecko: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1709355">https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1709355</a>)
WebKit: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/pull/55124">https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/pull/55124</a>)
Web developers: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121">https://github.com/web-platform-tests/interop/issues/1121</a>) The Interop 2026 WebTransport proposal received 28 👍 reactions. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
Other signals:
Ergonomics Ergonomics risk is low. reliability synchronously returns "pending" while connecting, and applications can await WebTransport.ready before reading its final value. The static supportsReliableOnly attribute enables capability detection before creating a connection.
Activation Activation risk is low. This is an additive API that does not change existing WebTransport behavior or require server changes. Developers can use standard feature detection and retain existing fallbacks for older browsers.
Security No new network capability or sensitive information is exposed. The attributes report whether an implementation or session supports exclusively reliable or unreliable WebTransport, which is already observable through the available WebTransport APIs. They expose no server data, credentials, addresses, or user-specific information.
WebView application risks
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? Low. This is an additive API surface and does not modify the behavior of existing WebTransport connections. WebView applications that do not use the attributes are unaffected
Debuggability The attributes can be inspected directly from JavaScript or the Chrome DevTools Console. Developers can inspect transport.reliability before and after transport.ready resolves and inspect WebTransport.supportsReliableOnly without creating a connection. No additional DevTools-specific support is required
Will this feature be supported on all six Blink platforms (Windows, Mac, Linux, ChromeOS, Android, and Android WebView)? Yes All Blink platforms on which WebTransport is supported. The implementation is in cross-platform Blink code.
Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests? Yes WPT coverage verifies that: • Initial "pending" state. • Transition after ready . • Web IDL exposure. Static attribute and initial state: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/reliability.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/reliability.https.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a> State after connection establishment: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/reliability.https.window.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/reliability.https.window.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a> IDL harness: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned">https://wpt.fyi/results/webtransport/idlharness.https.sub.any.html?label=experimental&label=master&aligned</a>
Flag name on about://flags chrome://flags/#enable-experimental-web-platform-features
Finch feature name WebTransportReliability
Rollout plan Will ship enabled for all users
Requires code in //chrome? False
Tracking bug <a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues/545636884">https://issues.chromium.org/issues/545636884</a>
Measurement Measure through Web Platform Test results, Interop 2026 WebTransport results, and developer feedback. No dedicated UMA metric is planned because this is an additive capability-reporting API that does not change network behavior.
Availability expectation Expected to become available across major browser engines as part of the W3C WebTransport specification. WebKit implements both attributes, while Firefox currently implements the per-session reliability attribute
Adoption expectation Expected to be adopted by WebTransport applications that use datagrams or need to operate across transports with different reliability capabilities.
Adoption plan Adoption is expected to happen organically as WebTransport applications use these attributes to select between reliable streams and unreliable datagrams.
Non-OSS dependencies
Does the feature depend on any code or APIs outside the Chromium open source repository and its open-source dependencies to function? No
Estimated milestones
Shipping on desktop 158
DevTrial on desktop 155
Shipping on Android 158
DevTrial on Android 155
Shipping on WebView 158
Anticipated spec changes
Open questions about a feature may be a source of future web compat or interop issues. Please list open issues (eg links to known github issues in the project for the feature specification) whose resolution may introduce web compat/interop risk (eg, changing to naming or structure of the API in a non-backward-compatible way). None. The attributes and WebTransportReliabilityMode values are already defined in the W3C WebTransport specification.

entry.content:
<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22Re%5C%3A+%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Re%5C%3A+Intent+to+Deprecate+and+Remove%5C%3A+Topics+API%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">Re: [blink-dev] Re: Intent to Deprecate and Remove: Topics API</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Mike+Taylor%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Mike Taylor</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20260930" rel="nofollow">Wed, 30 Sep 2026 09:22:25 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM2
On 9/30/26 8:29 a.m., Chris Harrelson wrote: </pre><blockquote style="border-left: #5555EE solid 0.2em; margin: 0em; padding-left: 0.85em"><pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM1</pre><pre>
On Thu, Sep 24, 2026 at 8:19 AM Yao Xiao <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="95ecf4fabbbbbbd5f6fde7faf8fce0f8bbfae7f2">[email protected]</a>> wrote:
Hi API Owners,
We have reached 1% on Stable (M153+) with no regressions or known breakage. The current usage is at 2% <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102">https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102</a>>. We would like to request approval to proceed with the staged deprecation rollout:
* 10% Stable: Hold for 2 weeks (through Oct 15) * 100% Stable: Target launch after Oct 15
Thanks for your consideration.
Best regards, Yao
On Wednesday, July 8, 2026 at 11:14:19 AM UTC-4 Alex Russell wrote:
LGTM3 on the condition that the rollout of this change is done progressively via Finch so we can monitor for breakage and roll back if things go sideways. Thanks for taking care not to break the web.
Best,
Alex
On Thursday, June 25, 2026 at 10:04:36 AM UTC-7 Chris Harrelson wrote:
LGTM2. Sorry for the delay.
On Thu, Jun 25, 2026 at 9:57 AM Yoav Weiss (@Shopify) <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="85fceae4f3f2e0abababc5e6edf7eae8ecf0e8abeaf7e2">[email protected]</a>> wrote:
LGTM1
On Fri, Jun 12, 2026 at 1:18 AM Yao Xiao <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="bdc4dcd2939393fdded5cfd2d0d4c8d093d2cfda">[email protected]</a>> wrote:
Hi API Owners, The Topics API was deprecated in Chrome-144 with a plan to remove it in Chrome-150. Currently the usage is 4.9% of page
loads.<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102">https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102</a>>We are proposing the following as next steps for removal and associated timelines: 1. M150: Remove all Ads API-related entries from Chrome settings and UI surfaces (e.g., chrome://settings/adPrivacy) via field trial. After this point, all API invocations for field-trial enabled browsers will always reject. Since the API can already be disabled for one of many reasons, scripts must already handle such rejections (or they’re already significantly broken).2. M152: Permanently remove the underlying implementation code for the API, and replace it with a lightweight stub API. The stub will remain removable via field trial.
3. M152 Canary/Beta: Begin a controlled rollout of the stub API removal via a field trial.4. M152 Stable: Assuming there are no regressions or breakage after reaching 1% stable, we will request additional approval for full removal at this stage.
At this time, we are seeking LGTMs for steps #2 and #3.
Thanks,
Yao
On Wednesday, November 12, 2025 at 11:36:22 AM UTC-5 Daniel Bratell wrote:
LGTM3 according to Vlad's plan.
/Daniel
On 2025-11-12 17:19, Chris Harrelson wrote: </pre><blockquote style="border-left: #5555EE solid 0.2em; margin: 0em; padding-left: 0.85em"><pre style="margin: 0em;"> LGTM2 with the same conditions Vlad mentioned.
On Wed, Nov 12, 2025 at 8:16 AM Vladimir Levin <<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="aadcc7da848484eac9c2d8c5c7c3dfc784c5d8cd">[email protected]</a>> wrote:
LGTM1 to deprecate. The plan to keep deprecation for 6 milestones also sounds good. Please come back after to this thread at a time when you think the removal can proceed. Since the amount of page loads is extremely high, we would like to reserve the right to pause the removal if this amount of page loads does not decrease substantially.
On Friday, November 7, 2025 at 1:12:36 PM UTC-5 Yao Xiao wrote:
Intent to Deprecate and Remove: Topics API
Contact emails
<a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="740d151b5a5a5a34171c061b191d01195a1b0613">[email protected]</a> <<a rel="nofollow" href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection#08716967262626486b607a6765617d6526677a6f">mailto:<span class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="2c554d430202026c4f445e434145594102435e4b">[email protected]</span></a>>
Explainer
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/patcg-individual-drafts/topics">https://github.com/patcg-individual-drafts/topics</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/patcg-individual-drafts/topics">https://github.com/patcg-individual-drafts/topics</a>>
Specification
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://patcg-individual-drafts.github.io/topics/">https://patcg-individual-drafts.github.io/topics/</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://patcg-individual-drafts.github.io/topics/">https://patcg-individual-drafts.github.io/topics/</a>>
Summary
The Topics API is a privacy-preserving web API to enable ad-targeting based on a person’s general browsing interests, without exposing their exact browsing history.
Following Chrome's announcement that the current approach to third-party cookies will be maintained, we are now planning to deprecate and remove the Topics API (along with other Privacy Sandbox APIs).
The following API surfaces will be affected:
*
The JavaScript function `document.browsingTopics()` will be removed.
*
The `browsingtopics` attribute on <iframe> and <img> elements will be ignored.
*
The `browsingTopics` option in the fetch() API's RequestInit will be a no-op.
*
Consequently, the `Sec-Browsing-Topics` request header will no longer be sent, and the `Observe-Browsing-Topics` response header will no longer be honored.
*
The "browsing-topics" and "interest-cohort" permissions policy features will be removed.
Blink component
Blink>TopicsAPI
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/u/1/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ETopicsAPI%22">https://issues.chromium.org/u/1/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ETopicsAPI%22</a>>
Web Feature ID
None
Motivation
Chrome has announced that the current approach to third-party cookies will be maintained. Given this, we expect adoption to decrease over time (currently at 13%
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102">https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102</a>>of page loads) as interest based advertising will remain possible in Chrome using third-party cookies. Further, other browser engines have not signaled interest in launching the API. See also the initial public proposal below.
Initial public proposal
<a rel="nofollow" href="https://privacysandbox.com/news/update-on-plans-for-privacy-sandbox-technologies/">https://privacysandbox.com/news/update-on-plans-for-privacy-sandbox-technologies/</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://privacysandbox.com/news/update-on-plans-for-privacy-sandbox-technologies/">https://privacysandbox.com/news/update-on-plans-for-privacy-sandbox-technologies/</a>>.
Possible breakage
Sites that rely on Topics API for targeting will experience utility impact.
If usage warrants, we will take steps to avoid any risk of page breakage, e.g. by temporarily retaining a stub implementation of `document.browsingTopics()` that mimics current behavior when a user has no topics to return. However, since Topics is not enabled by default for all users, sites should already be using feature detection, which makes the risks of breakage low.
Debuggability
N/A
Requires code in //chrome?
True
Estimated milestones
Deprecate in M144 and then remove in M150.
Currently, ~13%
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102">https://chromestatus.com/metrics/feature/timeline/popularity/5102</a>>of page loads use Topics API. These are driven by a small number of third-party ad tech scripts present on a large number of sites. We will continue to monitor usage as well as provide comprehensive updates on privacysandbox.google.com <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://goo.gle/ps-status">http://goo.gle/ps-status</a>>with the status of the API and deprecation plans.
We will also proactively work toward reducing usage to a low level once the intent is approved, including disallowing any new enrollment sign-ups, and contacting all enrolled sites that use the Privacy Sandbox APIs to inform them about the deprecation timelines.

<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22Re%5C%3A+%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+CSS+position%5C-visibility%5C%3Aanchor%5C%7Bs%5C%7D%5C-valid%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">Re: [blink-dev] Intent to Ship: CSS position-visibility:anchor{s}-valid</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22%27Mason+Freed%27+via+blink%5C-dev%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">'Mason Freed' via blink-dev</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20260929" rel="nofollow">Tue, 29 Sep 2026 07:48:03 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre> On Monday, September 28, 2026 at 11:32:35 AM UTC-7 Dan Clark wrote:
*> Is this feature fully tested by web-platform-tests <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md">https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/testing/web_platform_tests.md</a>>?*</pre><pre>
*> Yes> <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility">https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility">https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility</a>>*
The only of these tests I saw covering anchor-valid is this one: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position/position-visibility-anchor-valid.tentative.html">https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position/position-visibility-anchor-valid.tentative.html</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="http://Is%20this%20feature%20fully%20tested%20by%20web-platform-tests?%20Yes%20https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility">http://Is%20this%20feature%20fully%20tested%20by%20web-platform-tests?%20Yes%20https://wpt.fyi/results/css/css-anchor-position?label=master&label=experimental&aligned&q=position-visibility</a>> .
Maybe not too many tests are needed, but does this fully cover the behavior called out in the summary? "[The new version is] better defined to be clear that only the default anchor matters , resolving a lot of ambiguity"?
Sorry, I should have added to that response that my CL to implement the feature <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://crrev.com/c/8453827">https://crrev.com/c/8453827</a>> adds more testing.
E.g. the test shows that this is hidden: <div id="target2" class="target" style="top: anchor(--does-not-exist bottom);">target2</div>
But it'd be nice to include a case where position-anchor is unset but anchor() refers to an anchor name that actually does exist: <div id="target3" class="target" style="top: anchor(--a1 bottom);">target2</div>
I believe this is "Case 7" from the new position-visibility-anchor-valid-001.html test.
And maybe a similar set of checks with anchor-size().
This is indeed missing. I'll land another CL to add test cases for anchor-size like this - thanks for the suggestion.
Another case that seems important to have is an element that has a valid default anchor, but another anchor it depends on doesn't resolve. If I'm understanding correctly that would have resulted in the element being hidden in the original proposal <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/7758#issuecomment-1965540529">https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/7758#issuecomment-1965540529</a>>, but in the current proposal the element would be shown, since only the default anchor matters.
Also a good (missing) suggestion. I'll add it!
Thanks, Mason
Thanks, Dan

<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+Intent+to+Ship%5C%3A+Pause+media+playback+on+not%5C-visible+iframes%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] Intent to Ship: Pause media playback on not-visible iframes</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Chromestatus%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Chromestatus</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20260904" rel="nofollow">Fri, 04 Sep 2026 09:49:31 -0700</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Contact emails <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="e3848281918a868f8191cdcdcda38e8a80918c908c8597cd808c8e">[email protected]</a>, <a href="/cdn-cgi/l/email-protection" class="__cf_email__" data-cfemail="73000716055d5d5d331e1a10011c001c15075d101c1e">[email protected]</a> </pre><pre>
Explainer <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/IframeMediaPause/iframe_media_pausing.md">https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/IframeMediaPause/iframe_media_pausing.md</a>
Specification <a rel="nofollow" href="https://wicg.github.io/iframe-media-pausing">https://wicg.github.io/iframe-media-pausing</a>
Summary Adds a "media-playback-while-not-visible" permission policy to allow embedders to pause audible media playback of embedded iframes which are currently hidden - ie "display" property set to "none"; "visibility" property set to "hidden"; or zero-area (width or height equal to 0). While hidden, attempts made by the embedded iframe to render audible media will be blocked. When the frame is shown again the prohibitions should be lifted. This should allow developers to build more user-friendly experiences and to also improve the performance by letting the browser handle the playback of content that is not visible to users.
Blink component Blink>Media
Web Feature ID <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/web-platform-dx/web-features/issues/4292">https://github.com/web-platform-dx/web-features/issues/4292</a>
Motivation Web applications that host embedded media content via iframes may wish to respond to application input by temporarily hiding the media content. These applications may not want to unload the entire iframe when it's not rendered since it could generate user-perceptible performance and experience issues when showing the media content again. At the same time, the user could have a negative experience if the media continues to play and emit audio when not rendered. This proposal aims to provide web applications with the ability to control embedded media content in such a way that guarantees their users have a good experience when the iframe's render status is changed.
Initial public proposal No information provided
TAG review <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/1084">https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/1084</a>
TAG review status Issues addressed
Origin Trial Name media-playback-while-not-visible Permission Policy
Goals for experimentation Gather feedback from web developers and validate that the current prototype implementation works as expected. We have added telemetry to measure how the feature is being exercised by users: - HTMLMediaElement's: - # of pauses while hidden - # of pauses because got hidden during playback - WebAudio AudioContext's - # of interruptions while hidden - # of interruptions because got hidden during playback
Chromium Trial Name MediaPlaybackWhileNotVisiblePermissionPolicy
Origin Trial documentation link <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/IframeMediaPause/iframe_media_pausing.md">https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/MSEdgeExplainers/blob/main/IframeMediaPause/iframe_media_pausing.md</a>
WebFeature UseCounter name kMediaPlaybackWhileNotVisiblePermissionPolicy
Risks
Interoperability and Compatibility Firefox has already shown official support, although, we can't say for sure when other browsers are going to implement this feature. Safari also seems to be unofficially supportive: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10208#issuecomment-3060151372">https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10208#issuecomment-3060151372</a>
Gecko: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/1082">https://github.com/mozilla/standards-positions/issues/1082</a>)
WebKit: No signal (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/WebKit/standards-positions/issues/409">https://github.com/WebKit/standards-positions/issues/409</a>)
Web developers: Positive (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10208">https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/10208</a>) The community is supportive of resolving this problem using a permission policy. A commenter mentioned that the proposal fits well within the Permissions Policy API specification. They also agree that there is no workaround for this problem using current web API's. Feedback has been addressed to also include other invisibility scenarios like zero-area (height or width equal to 0) and to change the API name from "not-rendered" to "not-visible".
Other signals:
Ergonomics This feature will be used with other audio rendering API's, like HTMLMediaElement and Web Audio. This new behavior should only take effect if web pages explicitly opt-in by overriding the permission policy's default state. Moreover, once the permission policy is used, it should help Chromium to be more optimized by pausing audio rendering for content that is not visible for the user.
Activation Developers need to opt-in by setting "allow" property of an iframe. For example: <iframe src="<a rel="nofollow" href="https://foo.media.com&quot">https://foo.media.com&quot</a>; allow="media-playback-while-not-visible 'none'"></iframe>
WebView application risks
Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? None. This feature adds a new behavior that applications need to opt-in.
Debuggability No information provided
