entry.title: [blink-dev] PSA: URL/Location `protocol` setter no longer upgrades non-special URLs to special schemes
entry.summary: [blink-dev] PSA: URL/Location `protocol` setter no longer upgrades non-special URLs to special schemes
entry.content:
<div class="msgHead"> <h1> <span class="subject"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=subject:%22%5C%5Bblink%5C-dev%5C%5D+PSA%5C%3A+URL%5C%2FLocation+%60protocol%60+setter+no+longer+upgrades+non%5C-special+URLs+to+special+schemes%22&o=newest" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="name">[blink-dev] PSA: URL/Location `protocol` setter no longer upgrades non-special URLs to special schemes</span></a></span> </h1> <p class="darkgray font13"> <span class="sender pipe"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=from:%22Helmut+Januschka%22" rel="nofollow"><span itemprop="author" itemscope itemtype="http://schema.org/Person"><span itemprop="name">Helmut Januschka</span></span></a></span> <span class="date"><a href="/search?l=blink-dev@chromium.org&q=date:20261110" rel="nofollow">Tue, 10 Nov 2026 12:45:23 -0800</a></span> </p> </div><div itemprop="articleBody" class="msgBody">
<pre>Hi blink-dev,
A quick heads-up on a small spec-alignment fix landing shortly. What is changing</pre><pre>
Setting URL.protocol or Location.protocol to a special scheme (ftp, file, http, https, ws, wss) on a URL whose current scheme is non-special will become a silent no-op, matching <a rel="nofollow" href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-state">https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-state</a> step 2.1.2.
Example (before this change in Chromium):
const u = new URL("foo://example.com/"); u.protocol = "http"; u.href; // "<a rel="nofollow" href="http://example.com/&quot">http://example.com/&quot</a>; <-- Chrome today // "foo://example.com/" <-- spec, Firefox, Safari, Chrome after this change
HTMLAnchorElement / HTMLAreaElement .protocol setters go through the same path and are affected identically. Why
This closes the remaining half of a two-direction spec-alignment effort. Chromium already ships the mirror restriction (special -> non-special) since 2023 (crbug 1416018, crrev 61d4ebd@). Firefox shipped both directions in v117 (Aug 2023). WebKit ships it (bugs.webkit.org 229427). whatwg/url#674 asked to relax the rule and was closed WONTFIX in June 2026. Blink is currently the only engine that still permits this transition.
Spec origin: whatwg/url@5533c8d (Anne van Kesteren, 2015). Compat / interop impact
Expected to be negligible. The mirror direction (which was the more common of the two in the wild) measured 0.000139% on Beta / 0.0000346% on Dev when Hayato Ito ran a UseCounter in 2023 (crrev 54fc40d@), low enough that Intent to Ship was skipped. The direction being restricted now is rarer. Anyone who did depend on this pattern is already broken in Firefox and Safari, so live traffic is unlikely. Scope
Only the two JS-exposed setters are affected (URL.protocol, Location.protocol, including anchor/area element wrappers). Internal Blink callers of KURL::SetProtocol, favicon URL construction, URLPattern port canonicalization, mixed-content upgrade, WebSocket URL construction, form submission, resource loader, opt out via the new SpecialSchemeTransition enum and keep the legacy behavior. Flag / kill switch
DisallowSpecialSchemeOnNonSpecialUrl (default-on, RuntimeEnabledFeatures). just in case something goes south. Links
- CL: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://crrev.com/c/8734102">https://crrev.com/c/8734102</a> - Bug: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://crbug.com/40256682">https://crbug.com/40256682</a> - Spec: <a rel="nofollow" href="https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-state">https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#scheme-state</a> - whatwg/url#674 (WONTFIX): <a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/674">https://github.com/whatwg/url/issues/674</a> - Mirror-direction rollout (2023): crbug 1416018
Cheers, Helmut

*Summary*
WebTransport.getStats() provides asynchronous statistics for an existing connection: round-trip time measurements when available, an estimated sending rate when available, and counts of expired, lost, and dropped datagrams. Statistics remain accessible after the connection closes. Chromium does not currently expose connection byte or packet totals.
*Blink component*
Blink>Network>WebTransport
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22">https://issues.chromium.org/issues?q=customfield1222907:%22Blink%3ENetwork%3EWebTransport%22</a>>
*Web Feature ID*
webtransport <<a rel="nofollow" href="https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport">https://webstatus.dev/features/webtransport</a>>
*Motivation*
WebTransport applications need to distinguish connection latency, congestion, and datagram loss or expiration from application-side delays. A single asynchronous call exposes a snapshot of the existing connection's health to help developers adapt sending behavior and troubleshoot problems. It does not create a connection or change how application data is transmitted.

/No information provided/

<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/1212#issuecomment-5071009850">https://github.com/w3ctag/design-reviews/issues/1212#issuecomment-5071009850</a>

Issues addressed

None
*Risks*
*Interoperability and Compatibility*
This is an additive method on an existing WebTransport object: existing code is unaffected if it does not use the new method. Developers must check for method support and handle a rejection or missing dictionary members when working across browsers. Firefox and Safari expose getStats(), but implementation maturity and returned fields vary between all browsers. The WebTransport specification currently defines connection byte/packet counters (bytesSent, bytesSentOverhead, bytesAcknowledged, packetsSent, bytesLost, packetsLost, bytesReceived, packetsReceived) and atSendCapacity; Chromium does not expose these members. Applications should check for optional members rather than assume that every browser returns the same subset.
/Gecko/: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/158#apis">https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Mozilla/Firefox/Releases/158#apis</a>

/WebKit/: Shipped/Shipping (<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/WebKit-7625.2.8/Source/WebKit/NetworkProcess/webtransport/cocoa/NetworkTransportSessionCocoa.mm#L410-L413">https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/WebKit-7625.2.8/Source/WebKit/NetworkProcess/webtransport/cocoa/NetworkTransportSessionCocoa.mm#L410-L413</a>
<<a rel="nofollow" href="https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/WebKit-7625.2.8/Source/WebKit/NetworkProcess/webtransport/cocoa/NetworkTransportSessionCocoa.mm#L410-L413">https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/WebKit-7625.2.8/Source/WebKit/NetworkProcess/webtransport/cocoa/NetworkTransportSessionCocoa.mm#L410-L413</a>>) Safari 27.2 exposes WebTransport.getStats(), but its WebKit(7625.2.8) implementation returns default-initialized connection statistics. Developers also reported active WebTransport use and significant cross-engine differences.
/Other signals/:
*Ergonomics*
Values are asynchronous snapshots, not continuously updated measurements. RTT fields are in milliseconds; estimatedSendRate is in bits per second and can be null when no estimate is available.
*Activation*
There is no distinct activation risk identified for WebTransport.getStats(). Enabling it exposes an additive method; sites that do not call it keep their existing WebTransport behavior.
*Security*
The method returns aggregate connection information for a WebTransport object the caller already owns; it does not disclose payloads or peer credentials and does not add a new connection capability. RTT and estimated send rate can reveal characteristics of a user's network and help fingerprint or correlate activity. The WebTransport spec limits disclosure of connection and datagram counters on connections subject to pooling while permitting selected pooled-connection measurements such as RTT and estimated send rate.
*WebView application risks*
/Does this intent deprecate or change behavior of existing APIs, such that it has potentially high risk for Android WebView-based applications? /
Low. This is an additive API on existing WebTransport API and does not change connection establishment or network behavior.
*Debuggability*
Applications can inspect getStats() results from script or the DevTools Console. No dedicated DevTools connection-statistics UI is required for the API to work.

Yes
